entities.summary: Gerontius was a general of the Western Roman Empire, who initially supported the usurper Constantine III, later betraying him in favour of another usurper, Maximus of Hispania. Gerontius played a significant role in the Western Roman Empire's power struggles during the 4th century CE. He was a key figure in the intrigue surrounding the usurper Constantine III and was involved in the tumultuous politics of the time. Gerontius's actions had far-reaching consequences, influencing the trajectory of the Western Roman Empire's decline. The legacy of Gerontius can be seen in the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the late Roman Empire. Gerontius's betrayal of Constantine III is often cited as a pivotal moment in the empire's downward spiral. The impact of Gerontius's actions can still be felt today, with historians and scholars continuing to debate the intricacies of his role in the Western Roman Empire's collapse.
